newSounds: Retroflex stops t/d/n are said with the tongue tip curled back — you already have these from Telugu ట/ణ. Dental th/dh put the tongue tip on the teeth, not the English th. zh is a soft rzh; ng as in sing; ny as in canyon. Vowel length is meaningful: a/aa, i/ii, u/uu, e/ee, o/oo — hold the long ones.
rhythm: Syllable-timed, close to Telugu — every syllable gets one beat and stress is light, usually on the first syllable. Long vowels simply take a longer beat.
registerFirst: ninga, the polite 'you', with ungal for 'your'. The informal ni is for friends and family; stick with ninga until you are invited to drop it.
trap: Diglossia is the big one: spoken Tamil and written/formal Tamil are almost two different languages. Learn the spoken forms in this kit first — written eppadi irukkirirkal becomes spoken eppadi irukkinga, and the formal past/honorific endings are usually dropped in the street. Second trap: the short a is a light schwa (uh), so vanakkam is VAH-nak-kahm, not van-AH-kam; and dental th (tongue on teeth) is not English th.
